dataset.x: How do you like your steak prepared?

headline: In the steak-risk-survey data (raw.githubusercontent.com), answering "Rare" to "How do you like your steak prepared?" goes with answering "Yes" to "Do you ever smoke cigarettes?"
hypothesis: Respondents who order their steak rare are more likely to also smoke cigarettes.
mechanism: If risk taking is a general trait that carries across domains (Weber et al. 2002), tolerance for undercooked meat should travel with other risky habits such as smoking, which clusters with other risk behaviours (Petry & Oncken 2002).
question: Do people who like their steak rare take more everyday risks?

dataset.x: Do you have any children under 18?
dataset.y: In general, is itrude to bring a baby on a plane?

headline: In the flying-etiquette data (raw.githubusercontent.com), answering "Yes" to "Do you have any children under 18?" goes with answering "No, not at all rude" to "In general, is itrude to bring a baby on a plane?"
hypothesis: Respondents with children under 18 more often answer that bringing a baby on a plane is not at all rude.
mechanism: Parents perceive infant cries as less aversive and more interpretable than non-parents do (Green & Gustafson 1986; Green, Jones & Gustafson 1987), so a crying baby in the cabin should seem less of a breach of etiquette to them.
question: Do parents of minors judge bringing a baby on a plane as less rude than non-parents?

headline: In the candy-data data (raw.githubusercontent.com), higher "fruity" goes with lower "winpercent"
hypothesis: Candies flagged fruity win a smaller share of FiveThirtyEight's pairwise candy matchups.
mechanism: Chocolate is the most craved and liked sweet (Rozin et al. 1991; trait chocolate craving predicts implicit chocolate preference), and fruity candies are mostly non-chocolate, so they should lose most pairwise votes.
question: Do fruity candies lose head-to-head popularity contests against non-fruity candies?
